messages:
alex: Quick dump — ran a 90m protocol sweep comparing replay harness vs synthetic ramp for dedicated pools with burst-credit draining toggled. Putting top-line notes here, full CSV attached later.

mira: Can you paste top-line metrics? p95/p99, coldstart, and scale-up time?

alex: p95 steady: replay=85ms, synth=78ms; p99: replay=420ms, synth=360ms. Coldstart median: replay=4.2s, synth=2.3s. Scale-up (1->3 GPUs): replay=48s w/o KV priming, 26s with priming. Burst credits improved sustained throughput but increased p99 tail under high prefix variance.

juan: 4.2s coldstart for replay — were kernels different between runs?

alex: Yes — replay triggered a fallback kernel on ~30% of steps due to attention-length variance: matmul-v2 vs matmul-v1. Synth stuck to matmul-v1. When kernel flips mid-request we saw ~12-18% perf regression on those requests.

tasha: Do we have traces / flamegraphs? even a tiny nvprof snippet would help.

alex: Quick profiler snippet: 
```
Device 0: cudaMemcpyAsync 3.2ms
Kernel matmul-v1: avg 1.8ms
Kernel matmul-v2: avg 2.6ms
KV cache write: avg 0.4ms
KV cache read: avg 0.5ms
Attention kernel dispatch overhead: 0.15ms
```

mira: Re: KV priming — what primer length did you use? Was prefix cache warm across scale events?

alex: Priming=64 tokens per session for the baseline. With priming we warm many KV buckets so coldstart drops ~1.6s on median. Note: priming increases initial token cost (extra tokens emitted/charged) — tradeoff for tail. On scale events the cache was mostly cold unless priming ran.

ev an: For apples-to-apples, did you normalize batch shapes and seq len distribution between synth and replay? That often skews kernel selection.

alex: Yes — we forced the same batch/seq histogram via the harness config. However replay still had real prefix skew and micro-variance that flips kernel selection at runtime. Synth used statically-clamped seq-lengths so kernel stayed consistent.

juan: Any obvious perf regressions tied to recent runtime commits?

alex: We saw a small regression after the attention-dispatch refactor (PR #4521) — it added a safety-path that picks matmul-v2 for certain ragged lengths. On synthetic loads the safety-path isn't hit, but replay exercises it.

mira: Actionable items?

juan: 1) Add kernel-hinting heuristic to prefer the kernel likely to remain stable for the expected seq-length histogram.

tasha: 2) Expose priming length per-pool and try priming=128 for critical pools (config toggle).

ev an: 3) Update autoscale policy: pre-warm an extra node when burst credits are available and predicted ramp > 2x.

sre-bot: incident-snapshot: burst-credit drain observed at 2026-02-12T15:02Z; p99 latency spike 2.1x; logs: http://internal/logs/abcd (retention 30d) :warning: 

alex: I'll run a follow-up A/B: 30m runs with kernel-hint + priming=128 + prewarm=1. Will post CSV tomorrow.

mira: Also add a clamp in the replay harness to avoid attention window oscillations that flip kernels mid-request (cheap guard).

juan: If prewarm reduces scale-up from 48s to <30s we can safely reduce SLA buffer for dedicated pools (say 15s->10s) and save costs.

tasha: Tagging infra: @infra-team can you add a per-pool prewarm toggle and a priming-config flag?

alex: Command I used to run the harness: 
```
./run_harness --mode=replay --seed=42 --priming=128 --kernel-hint=prefer-stable --target-pools=dedicated-prod-1 --duration=1800
```

mira: Great, please upload the results CSV to S3 and mark which runs used burst-credit=true/false.

alex: Uploaded results: s3://redwood-bench/proto-sweep/1829992222/results.csv (contains per-request kernel id, latency, kv-hit flags)

ev an: FYI when burst credits >50% used our scheduler allowed noisy co-tenants onto the same host which increased p99 — we need an isolation flag for critical pools.

juan: Agreed. Add isolation flag + prioritize prewarm for pools with isolation=true.

alex: Follow-ups: I'll run the A/B and open PRs: kernel-hinting + replay-clamp + per-pool priming. Will link PRs in this thread.

mira: Thanks — good progress, clear next steps.

tasha: Nice thread, thanks alex.
